No, that is not true. In Switzerland, only Swiss citizens have the right to vote in federal elections. Persons with a C permit (settlement permit), like other foreign residents, do not have the right to vote in federal elections.

Voting rights in Switzerland are tied to Swiss citizenship. Foreign residents, regardless of the type of residence permit (such as B, C, or L permits), do not participate in federal elections, referendums, or initiatives at the federal level. Some Swiss cantons and municipalities may grant voting rights in local or municipal elections to foreign residents under certain conditions, but this is not applicable at the federal level.
